parsed.claim: HasExponentialBound allows an arbitrary prefactor C. The sequence 2·exp(-n) satisfies it, yet it violates every pure bound exp(-c·n) with c>0 at n=0, because the value there is 2 > 1. So the definition is formally weaker than a pure exp(-c·n) bound, at least at n=0.
parsed.lean:
theorem probe_hasExp_weaker :
    QuantumParallelRepetition.HasExponentialBound (fun n : ℕ => 2 * Real.exp (-(1:ℝ) * (n:ℝ))) ∧
    ¬ ∃ c : ℝ, 0 < c ∧ ∀ n : ℕ,
      (fun n : ℕ => 2 * Real.exp (-(1:ℝ) * (n:ℝ))) n ≤ Real.exp (-c * (n:ℝ)) := by
  refine ⟨⟨1, one_pos, 2, two_pos, fun n => le_refl _⟩, ?_⟩
  rintro ⟨c, hc, h⟩
  have := h 0
  norm_num at this
